data_note: Built from publisher RSS metadata (titles + teaser text). `coverage_window_hours` is the default (40h); several feeds use a longer `rollingHours` (see `scripts/build-digest.mjs`) so rows align with what is still on each publisher’s listing pages. Commercial Observer keeps its retail category + hub supplement; TRD adds a New York–filtered global retail tag feed. PincusCo uses the live site feed only (`/category/retail/feed/` is stale). **CRE Daily** retail briefs come from `credaily.com/sectors/retail/feed/`. **WSJ** is the Dow Jones real-estate feed with lifestyle and opinion dropped. **The New York Times** keeps real-estate and property stories only. **Traded** is commercial deal briefs from its news listing. Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group signed a 10-year, roughly 8,000-square-foot lease at 21 West Eighth Street in Greenwich Village.

ColorPop Workshop , an art studio offering children ages 3 to 12 a variety of classes, has inked a 1,000-square-foot deal at the base of Related Companies ’ 450 Washington Street in Manhattan’s Tribeca neighborhood, according to tenant broker Meridian Retail Leasing .

A flurry of leases and rising rents have defined the area in 2026, according to the Real Estate Board of New York (REBNY) ’ s most recent Brooklyn retail report, shared exclusively with Commercial Observer.

Host Hotels Rounds Out $202M Brooklyn Hotel Buy With $29M Retail, Parking Acquisition: Host Hotels & Resorts has secured three retail spaces and an indoor parking area at its newly acquired hotel asset in Brooklyn’s Dumbo neighborhood. items.headline: Houston Retail Demand Tops New Supply for First Time in a Year
items.summary: Houston retail net absorption of 399,400 SF beat 339,800 SF of deliveries in Q3, the first quarter in 12 months in which demand topped new supply, according to Colliers. Rents rose 7.9% to $22.06 per SF, a fourth straight record, and sales volume climbed 18% to more than $953M, though vacancy edged up to 5.8% and leasing slowed. Construction jumped 48% to 4.4M SF, so a new supply wave could test a market where restaurant, fitness, medical and grocery demand is well diversified.…

items.headline: Simon Pursues Zaytinya Eviction Over $2M in Unpaid Rent
items.summary: Simon filed an unlawful detainer complaint on Nov. 17 over Zaytinya at Stanford Shopping Center in Palo Alto, alleging nearly $2 million in unpaid rent and charges. The 10-year lease began at $96,834 a month plus percentage rent of 13.625% to 21.5% of sales, and Simon seeks over $3,000 daily in damages from Dec. 1. Other food tenants at the center have also struggled, including a True Food Kitchen bankruptcy, even as Simon reports 96.5% occupancy across its U.S. malls and outlets.…

items.headline: Brookfield Marks Catalyst Brands Stake Down 50% to $276M
items.summary: A Brookfield Corp. property unit’s third-quarter filing carries its holding in the JCPenney and Aéropostale parent at $276M, half the prior $551M. The stake traces to a 2020 deal with Simon Property to buy JCPenney for $800M, partly to keep big anchor spaces in their malls from going dark. The markdown arrived with a $430M drop in the value of Brookfield’s mall portfolio, a sign that pressure on secondary retail assets persists. Key Takeaways Owning your tenants is getting expensive for Brookfield.…

items.headline: This Holiday Season, New York City Retail’s Split Recovery Reaches a Critical Point
items.summary: The last mile is the hardest, and New York City’s retail sector is flagging near the finish line. Peter Braus, president and principal owner of Lee & Associates NYC, sees a retail market balancing two extremes. On one hand, it’s becoming increasingly hard to find the right space in the right area. One of Braus’s current clients, a “very strong” Italian brand seeking a New York City home in SoHo or along Madison Avenue, is in an especially competitive spot.…

items.headline: Los Tacos No. 1 to Open at 900 Third Avenue in Midtown East
items.summary: A popular Mexican street taco chain in New York City is opening yet another location in Manhattan. Los Tacos No. 1 , which debuted at Chelsea Market in 2013, has signed a 15-year, 7,105-square-foot lease at the base of Elecor Properties ’ 900 Third Avenue in Midtown East, according to landlord broker Cushman & Wakefield . The taqueria’s new spot on the corner of Third Avenue and East 54th Street will open in mid-2027 and replace a shuttered Bank of America branch.…

items.headline: London Jazz Club Inks 12K-SF Lease at 250 Mercer Street in NoHo
items.summary: It’s just a noisy hall where there’s a nightly brawl, and all that jazz . Famed London jazz club Ronnie Scott’s has signed a 20-year, 11,739-square-foot lease at 250 Mercer Street in Manhattan’s NoHo neighborhood. Ronnie Scott’s opened in 1959 in London’s Soho district and was the first U.K.-based club to regularly host American jazz legends such as Ella Fitzgerald and Miles Davis. Now, the business plans to build out a premier jazz club on Manhattan’s Mercer Street, in what will be its first U.S. location.…

Shin Jidai, founded in 2010, currently operates approximately 200 casual pubs, known as izakayas, across Japan.…

items.headline: California Retail Braces for 2027 Costs as AI Use Grows
items.summary: Ed Del Beccaro of TRI Commercial/CORFAC says value-focused shopping continues in California, while upper-income cities like Palo Alto and Walnut Creek still support travel, beauty and experiential spending. Retailers expect 2027 costs to rise on mandated minimum wage increases, food tariffs and higher fuel prices, while sales are projected to stay flat or shrink, particularly at restaurants.…
